input_check.note: These checks test physical consistency (rigid 3-D scene, motion matching GPS, metadata agreeing with telemetry). They can expose fabricated or mismatched inputs, but no software can certify that footage is genuine.

kpis.label: Median consecutive overlap
kpis.detail: Overlap between each kept frame and the previous one, measured by verified optical flow.

kpis.label: Pairs below 50% overlap
kpis.detail: Each such pair is a likely break in the SfM match graph.

kpis.label: Frames selected
kpis.detail: from 3029 video frames

kpis.label: Projected selection time, 10-min 4K clip
kpis.detail: analysis 44 s (149 ms per kept frame x 297 frames) + decode 235 s (39.55 s here, scaled to 10 min of 4K; software decode — hardware decode or keyframe seeking changes this). Estimate: verify on real 4K footage.

kpis.label: Analysis cost per kept frame
kpis.detail: Flow + photometric verification + blur metrics, excluding decode.

kpis.label: Frames decoded / frames in video
kpis.detail: The predictive stride should decode a small fraction of the video.

processes.what: Picks the frames to reconstruct from, targeting a set overlap between neighbours so every surface is seen from several angles without processing thousands of near-identical frames.
processes.covers: Measured overlap between consecutive kept frames, how many frames were kept, and the selection time against its budget.
processes.lacks: It cannot know whether the flight itself covered the whole site: a strip the drone never flew over is reported later, as a gap.

kpis.label: Rejected / evaluated
kpis.detail: 0 of 165 evaluated frames rejected (0 for directional blur).

kpis.label: Coverage warnings (reject runs)
kpis.detail: Runs of consecutive rejected frames — flight segments with reduced coverage.

processes.what: Rejects frames whose motion blur would push wrong geometry into the reconstruction, and marks mildly soft frames for sharpening instead.
processes.covers: The share of frames rejected, and whether the sharpness threshold adapted to the clip rather than being fixed.
processes.lacks: Blur is judged on the whole frame, so a sharp frame with one blurred moving object is kept; the moving object is handled by dynamic masking instead.

kpis.label: Source and sensors found
kpis.detail: ignored 18 unmapped ST 0601 tags: 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 82, 83, 84, 85; shifted by +1.30 s: offset measured by the input check

kpis.label: Selected frames with a GPS fix
kpis.detail: Zero means a scale-free, non-georeferenced model (§4.2 path 4).

kpis.label: Telemetry span / video duration
kpis.detail: A mismatch suggests the sidecar belongs to a different clip or is time-offset.

processes.what: Reads the position log that came with the video, in whatever format it arrived, and puts it on the same clock as the frames.
processes.covers: Which optional inputs were present (GPS, barometric altitude, attitude, focal length, RTK) and how many fixes were aligned to frames.
processes.lacks: It records what the telemetry claims; the accuracy of the GPS itself is measured later, when the reconstructed camera path is compared against it.

kpis.label: Frames requiring correction
kpis.detail: 25 of 50 frames had visible blocking.

kpis.label: Keypoints vetoed on block grid
kpis.detail: SIFT/FAST keypoints discarded on compression block boundary.

kpis.label: Blockiness reduction on corrected frames
kpis.detail: Mean score before: 1.877, after: 1.335.

processes.what: Finds and softens compression blocking, the square edges a heavily compressed video leaves, which would otherwise be matched as if they were real corners.
processes.covers: How many frames showed blocking, and the measured reduction on the frames that were corrected, before and after.
processes.lacks: It measures the blocking signal, not the downstream benefit; that is measured separately by the degradation benchmark.

kpis.label: Low-light frames
kpis.detail: 0 of 50 frames triggered low-light path (§5.4 accuracy note).

kpis.label: Mean shadow coverage per frame
kpis.detail: Peak per-frame shadow coverage: 28.7%. High coverage means either a genuinely shadowed scene or an over-firing detector; separating the two needs ground truth (S2-3).

kpis.label: Blown-out pixels in conditioned frames
kpis.detail: Peak per-frame saturation: 1.5%.

kpis.label: Frames with exposure clamped
kpis.detail: 0 of 50 frames hit a gain bound; their exposure was not fully normalised. Unbounded, the chain would have reached gain 0.883 — far from 1.0 means per-link error is compounding, not that the scene changed.

kpis.label: Exposure gain span across sequence
kpis.detail: Span the chain asked for before clamping: 0.207. Large values mean auto-exposure drift, a compounding chain, or both.

kpis.label: Exposure chain links rejected
kpis.detail: A rejected link means irrecoverable lighting change between adjacent frames.

processes.what: Keeps brightness consistent across the flight, lifts shadow detail and marks shadowed pixels so they carry less weight when surfaces are matched.
processes.covers: The exposure correction actually applied, whether any frame was driven to its limit, the share of the frame in shadow and the share of blown-out pixels in the written frames.
processes.lacks: Shadow detection has no per-pixel ground truth on real footage, so its precision is measured on synthetic scenes rather than on this clip.

kpis.label: Frames containing dynamic objects
kpis.detail: 0/50 frames had movers. Methods: semantic.

processes.what: Masks out things that move, such as vehicles, so they neither anchor the camera solution nor leave smeared geometry in the model.
processes.covers: The masked share of each frame and how many frames contained movers.
processes.lacks: Without a semantic model installed it falls back to geometric consistency, which catches movement but cannot name the object.

kpis.label: GPS fixes rejected as outliers
kpis.detail: Envelope: 1, median: 1, from 103 fixes.

kpis.label: Fixes after Kalman smoothing
kpis.detail: Fixes with a finite smoothed position estimate.

kpis.label: Altitude source
kpis.detail: baro+gps_complementary is best; GPS-only is noisier but keeps an absolute datum; baro_relative_only leaves the vertical datum unknown, which breaks absolute georeferencing downstream.

kpis.label: RTK/PPK detected
kpis.detail: GPS weight: 1.0x with RTK.

kpis.label: Max observed speed (m/s)
kpis.detail: Measured across all accepted GPS fixes before smoothing.

processes.what: Removes impossible jumps from the position log and smooths the rest, so the track handed to georeferencing is physically plausible.
processes.covers: Outliers removed, fixes smoothed, the altitude source chosen and the fastest speed observed.
processes.lacks: Smoothing cannot add information the receiver never had; residual GPS error still sets the absolute placement of the final model.

kpis.detail: views per sparse point: more views, better triangulated

processes.what: Works out where the camera was for every frame by matching the same features across frames, then refines all positions together against the GPS track.
processes.covers: The share of frames placed, how well the matched points reproject, how long each feature track survives, and whether the solution broke into pieces.
processes.lacks: A high score here means the solution is internally consistent; agreement with the real world is the separate GPS check below.

kpis.label: Height above ground vs telemetry

processes.what: Checks the reconstruction against the world: camera positions against the GPS track, and the computed flying height against what the telemetry reported.
processes.covers: Camera-centre agreement with GPS in metres, flying-height error as a percentage, the focal length source, and a gate that caps the score if the solution disagrees with GPS.
processes.lacks: GPS is the yardstick here, so this measures agreement with the telemetry, not absolute truth; independent ground truth is the lidar comparison in Accuracy.

kpis.label: Views confirming each point
kpis.detail: 2,258,965 back-projected, 2,168,065 kept after the multi-view check

processes.what: Runs a learned depth model over the frames and pins its output to the measured geometry, adding detail in areas where stereo matching alone is thin.
processes.covers: How many frames the depth was successfully anchored on, how tightly it agreed with the measured points, and how many views confirm each fused point.
processes.lacks: Learned depth is only accepted where it agrees with measurement; where it disagrees it is refused, which protects accuracy but limits how much it can add.

processes.what: Turns the confirmed depth into a dense point cloud, then a continuous surface, then paints the photographs back onto it.
processes.covers: Point and face counts, mesh soundness, whether texturing succeeded, and the share of the texture that carries real image data.
processes.lacks: Face count describes detail, not correctness; correctness is measured against the reference surface in Accuracy.

processes.covers: Wall-clock time per step and the budget handed on to the next step.
processes.lacks: Times are specific to the machine that ran them; the projection column re-states them for a 10-minute clip on this same hardware.

processes.what: Labels every part of the scene by how well it was actually observed: how many cameras saw it and from how wide an angle.
processes.covers: The zone map itself, the share of the scene in each zone, and the view and angle statistics behind the labels.
processes.lacks: Zones describe observation quality, not the error in metres; the two are compared in Accuracy, where the zones are shown to rank error correctly.

processes.what: Fills thinly observed areas using learned depth that is scaled and shifted to match the well-observed surface next to it, and never allowed to overwrite measured geometry.
processes.covers: Frames accepted versus refused, the error on points deliberately held back from the fit, and a re-check that no measured voxel was overwritten.
processes.lacks: Filled surface is inferred, not measured; it is labelled as such in the model so a user can exclude it.

processes.what: Reports what was reconstructed and, just as importantly, draws the outline of everything the cameras never saw instead of inventing it.

processes.lacks: A gap is honest reporting, not a fix; closing one needs either another pass over that ground or an assumption the system refuses to make.

processes.covers: Every format verified by reading it back, the point cloud's classification, and the confidence and zone layers travelling with the model.

processes.what: Carries the coverage figure measured during occlusion handling into the exported products, so the delivered files state how much of the scene they actually describe.
processes.covers: The reconstructed percentage and the raster and vector products that record it.
processes.lacks: Coverage counts ground the cameras saw; ground outside the flight path is a flight-planning question, not a reconstruction one.

projection.basis: Times scale with the number of frames kept, which scales with the length of the flight, so each measured time is multiplied by 10 minutes divided by this clip's length. Accuracy and coverage figures are properties of the flight and do not change with clip length.

coverage.source: Stage 3 zone map (zone 1 + zone 2 of the ground the cameras saw)

zones.note: zone 1 = measured, >= zone1_min_views at a sufficient angle; zone 2 = thin or monocular (anchored, weight < zone 1); zone 3 = never observed, listed in gaps.geojson, never filled

reference.vertical: reference heights converted WGS 84 / UTM zone 17N + EGM96 height -> WGS 84 / UTM zone 17N: +0.000 m here

accuracy.note: vertical errors = our point height minus the reference surface under it; zone 3 is never measured (no points), so it has no accuracy figure by construction. 'local' removes each 100 m tile's own 3D offset: what remains is shape error at that scale

limitations: Speed: 7.1 min for 1.7 min of video projects to 42 min for a 10-minute video against the §9 target of 15 min (device cuda; S4-8).
Camera centres agree with GPS to 3.346 m RMS: absolute position is limited by the telemetry; relative distances within Zone 1 are more reliable.
30.8% of the ground the cameras saw was never observed (Zone 3): flagged in gaps.geojson and the viewer, never filled, excluded from accuracy.
The single-pass simulation needs a multi-strip survey; not run for this report.

obj: The textured surface as plain text geometry: the most widely accepted mesh format, opened by every 3D package.
ply: Every reconstructed point with its colour and its per-point confidence and zone layers.
las: The survey-industry point format, classified into ground, above ground and low noise, and tiled for large sites.
geotiff: A height model and a true-colour orthophoto, both carrying the coordinate system so they drop straight into any GIS.
glb: The web and game-engine format: geometry and texture in one file, used by the viewer on this page.
fbx: The interchange format for Blender, 3ds Max, Maya and Unreal.
